canonical_definition: Object Detection is the task of identifying and localizing objects within visual data (e.g., images or videos), typically producing outputs such as object class labels and spatial coordinates. It is often evaluated using metrics like Average Precision (AP) on benchmarks such as COCO, with variants addressing specialized contexts like camouflaged object detection (CAMO, COD10K) or multimodal hallucination assessment (POPE). This behavior reflects perceptual capability in vision-language models, supports downstream tasks like screen understanding via OCR/icon detection, and serves as a foundational skill in systems combining specialist modules (e.g., segmentation, depth estimation) for complex reasoning.
